questions.stem: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. One of the alternate angles is $65°$. What is the other alternate angle?
questions.explanation: Alternate angles between parallel lines are equal, so the other angle is also $65°$.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. A pair of co-interior (same-side) angles are formed. One is $130°$. What is the other?
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles between parallel lines sum to $180°$: $180° - 130° = 50°$.

questions.stem: Corresponding angles formed by a transversal crossing parallel lines are:
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles (in the same position at each intersection) are equal when lines are parallel.

questions.stem: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. One angle is $(3x + 15)°$ and its corresponding angle is $72°$. What is $x$?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal: $3x + 15 = 72$, so $3x = 57$ and $x = 19$.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Angle $a = 110°$. What is the co-interior angle to $a$?
Which pair of angles are NOT equal when a transversal crosses parallel lines?
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles are supplementary (sum to $180°$), not equal. Alternate, corresponding, and vertically opposite angles are all equal.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. An alternate angle is $(2x + 10)°$ and its pair is $(3x - 20)°$. What is the size of each angle?
questions.explanation: Alternate angles are equal: $2x + 10 = 3x - 20$, so $x = 30$. Each angle is $2(30) + 10 = 70°$.
